title: Move an Express in-process job runner to Amazon SQS and AWS Lambda
description: An Express app that runs jobs in the request process, then the same app enqueuing to Amazon SQS and running the steps in an AWS Lambda consumer. No API change.

introBox.headline: How it works
text: An Express service that runs background jobs in the request process is tied to that process: a deploy, scale-in or crash strands every in-flight job, and the box is sized for the work rather than the traffic. This pattern shows that app (before/) and the same app with the work moved to Amazon SQS and an AWS Lambda consumer (after/).

In the after/ version the API keeps the same /v1 routes, job ids and status endpoint, but POST /v1/jobs writes a PENDING row to a DynamoDB jobs table, sends one SQS message, and returns. A separate Lambda is triggered by the queue and runs the identical step code, updating the same row to DONE or FAILED.

SQS gives you what the in-process worker could not: redelivery of unacknowledged messages after the visibility timeout, a dead-letter queue for poison messages, partial batch failure so only failed messages retry, and independent scaling of the API and the worker.
The API contract does not change, so clients are untouched. The after/ half reuses the same table and routes, and the before/ folder is included only for comparison and is not deployed.

The handlers have local tests that invoke them with API Gateway proxy events and an SQS event against mocked AWS clients, so the idempotent enqueue, reserved-word aliasing and stale-error clearing can be verified without deploying.
